title: Ice Cream 1.5L

adjustment.analysis: No events, promotions, or price changes in the target week. The baseline already reflects a strong upward trend (69.4% 13-week trend) and seasonal lift (mean_52=55.0 vs mean_13=48.6). Past Memorial Day (week before) showed only a noise-adjusted x1.0 effect. No promotion history at current price (6.41), and recent non-promo weeks (2026-05-04 to 05-11) average 45 units, near baseline. The classical uplift model’s x1.0 is consistent with evidence. No driver justifies adjustment.

brief:
PRODUCT: Ice Cream 1.5L | category Frozen | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-05-18 to 2026-05-24 (next week)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 6.41 (+0.0% vs regular price 6.41)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 51.3 | 5%-95%: 26.9 - 79.1 | 10%-90%: 39.7 - 72.9

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-31% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
